trusted_entities.assumption: Execution client trusts authenticated Engine API calls from paired consensus client to reflect canonical fork choice view. Methods include engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV1/V2/V3, engine_newPayloadV1/V2/V3/V4, and engine_getPayloadV1/V2/V3/V4/V5 per execution-apis specification. [S3] [S4] Geth implements ConsensusAPI in eth/catalyst/api.go with authenticated RPC namespace. [S1] Sources: [S1] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:48-58, [S3] https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/, [S4] https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/interacting-with-geth/rpc
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Hostile Engine API peer can inject invalid payload attributes or fork choice states, causing chain reorganizations to malicious branches, liveness failures via incorrect finalization, or construction of invalid blocks that get rejected by honest network peers. [S1] Geth tracks invalid blocks ephemerally (never persisted) with hit-count eviction after 128 references to allow retry. [S1] Sources: [S1] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:60-125

trusted_entities.assumption: Node operators trust locally configured fork activation block numbers and timestamps in params/config.go to match network consensus rules. [S5] Mainnet activations include London (EIP-1559) at block 12965000, Paris (Merge) at TTD 58750000000000000000000, Shanghai at timestamp 1681338455, Cancun at 1710338135, Prague at 1746612311, and Osaka at 1764798551. [S5] Sources: [S5] ./params/config.go:40-76
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Stale or incorrect fork configuration causes rejection of valid post-fork transactions (e.g., EIP-1559 dynamic fee, EIP-4844 blob, EIP-7702 setcode transactions), inability to process blocks containing new opcodes or precompiles, mempool acceptance of invalid transactions, or consensus splits from canonical network. [S5] [S6] Sources: [S5] ./params/config.go:894-916, [S6] ./core/txpool/validation.go:74-87

trusted_entities.assumption: Geth assumes P2P peers are untrusted and validates all received blocks, transactions, and messages before state incorporation. [S7] ETH68/ETH69 protocol implements fork ID validation, message size limits (10 MB max), and sync challenge verification. [S7] Blocks undergo full validation via BlockValidator.ValidateBody and ValidateState. [S8] Sources: [S7] ./eth/protocols/eth/protocol.go:30-60, [S8] ./core/block_validator.go:50-140
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Malicious peers cannot directly corrupt node state due to validation gates, but can waste resources via DoS (sending oversized messages, invalid blocks), eclipse attacks (isolating node from honest network), or tx censorship (withholding valid transactions). [S7] [S9] Geth enforces max message size and peer reputation tracking. [S9] Sources: [S7] ./eth/protocols/eth/protocol.go:30-60, [S9] ./eth/handler.go:100-250

trusted_entities.assumption: Geth trusts secp256k1 ECDSA signature scheme for transaction authentication. [S10] Signature verification via types.Sender() in validation.go recovers public key and derives address. [S10] Replay protection via EIP-155 chainID in signature. [S11] Sources: [S10] ./core/txpool/validation.go:115-118, [S11] ./core/types/transaction_signing.go:40-80
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Compromise of secp256k1 allows attacker to forge transactions from arbitrary accounts, draining all funds and executing unauthorized state changes. Requires cryptographic break of elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem or collision in keccak256 hash. [S10] Sources: [S10] ./core/txpool/validation.go:115-118

trusted_entities.assumption: All network nodes compute identical base fee per block using deterministic algorithm: baseFee_new = max(0, baseFee + baseFee * (gasUsed - gasTarget) / gasTarget / 8). [S12] Implementation in consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go. [S12] Sources: [S12] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-70
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Non-deterministic base fee calculation causes consensus divergence as different nodes compute different base fees, rejecting each other's valid blocks. Manifests as chain split. Geth validates base fee in VerifyEIP1559Header. [S12] [S13] Sources: [S12] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-70, [S13] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:80-95

trusted_entities.assumption: Precompiled contracts at addresses 0x01-0x11 implement cryptographic operations deterministically with fixed gas costs. [S14] Includes ECRECOVER (0x01), SHA256 (0x02), RIPEMD160 (0x03), Identity (0x04), ModExp (0x05), BN256 curves (0x06-0x08), Blake2F (0x09), KZG point evaluation (0x0a), and BLS12-381 operations (0x0b-0x11). [S14] Sources: [S14] ./core/vm/contracts.go:80-150
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Non-deterministic precompile execution causes state divergence. Incorrect gas costs enable DoS via underpriced expensive operations. Cryptographic vulnerabilities in precompile implementations (e.g., KZG, BLS) could break EIP-4844 blob verification or future Verkle proofs. [S14] [S15] Sources: [S14] ./core/vm/contracts.go:80-150, [S15] ./crypto/kzg4844/kzg4844.go:40-90

trusted_entities.assumption: State root in block header is cryptographically binding commitment to world state computed via Merkle Patricia Trie. [S16] Geth validates state root after transaction execution in BlockValidator.ValidateState. [S17] Trie implementation in triedb/database.go. [S16] Sources: [S16] ./core/state/statedb.go:650-700, [S17] ./core/block_validator.go:140-180
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: State root mismatch between nodes prevents block acceptance, causing chain halt. Collision in keccak256 or trie construction bug allows forging state roots for arbitrary states, enabling theft of all assets. Geth rejects blocks with incorrect state roots. [S17] Sources: [S17] ./core/block_validator.go:140-180

trusted_entities.assumption: Every EVM opcode has fixed or bounded gas cost to prevent infinite loops and ensure execution terminates. [S18] Gas metering in vm/gas_table.go and vm/interpreter.go. [S18] Dynamic costs for memory expansion, storage access (SLOAD/SSTORE), and calls. [S19] Sources: [S18] ./core/vm/gas_table.go:50-150, [S19] ./core/vm/interpreter.go:120-200
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Underpriced opcodes enable DoS by executing expensive operations cheaply (e.g., infinite loop costs less than block gas limit). Overpriced opcodes make legitimate operations unaffordable. Gas metering bugs in EIP-2929 (cold/warm storage) or EIP-1884 (SLOAD cost increase) caused historical issues. [S18] [S20] Sources: [S18] ./core/vm/gas_table.go:50-150, [S20] ./core/vm/operations_acl.go:30-80

trusted_entities.assumption: Blob transactions include KZG polynomial commitments verified via point evaluation precompile at 0x0a. [S21] Validation in txpool/validation.go:190-199 checks commitment matches blob hash. [S21] Trusted setup ceremony parameters embedded in crypto/kzg4844. [S22] Sources: [S21] ./core/txpool/validation.go:190-199, [S22] ./crypto/kzg4844/kzg4844.go:50-100
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Invalid KZG commitments accepted into mempool or blocks allow data availability failures where blob data doesn't match commitment, breaking rollup security. Compromise of trusted setup allows forging proofs. Geth validates all blob commitments before pool admission and block import. [S21] [S23] Sources: [S21] ./core/txpool/validation.go:190-199, [S23] ./core/block_validator.go:100-120

trusted_entities.assumption: Private keys stored in keystore (accounts/keystore/) are secured by user-provided passphrase. [S24] Geth never transmits private keys over network or Engine API. [S24] Keys encrypted via scrypt KDF with configurable parameters. [S25] Sources: [S24] ./accounts/keystore/keystore.go:50-100, [S25] ./accounts/keystore/passphrase.go:40-90
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Compromised private keys grant full control over associated accounts, enabling theft of funds and execution of arbitrary transactions. Weak passphrase or keystore file theft exposes keys. Geth documentation warns against unlocking accounts over HTTP RPC due to attack surface. [S4] [S24] Sources: [S4] https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/interacting-with-geth/rpc, [S24] ./accounts/keystore/keystore.go:50-100

trusted_entities.entity: System Contracts (Beacon Root, History Storage, Withdrawal/Consolidation Queues)
trusted_entities.assumption: System contracts at predefined addresses (EIP-4788: 0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02, EIP-2935: 0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935, EIP-7002: 0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002, EIP-7251: 0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251) are called via system transactions with correct ABI. [S26] Implemented in core/state_processor.go:260-400. [S26] Sources: [S26] ./core/state_processor.go:260-400
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Incorrect system contract calls or ABI mismatches cause block processing failures. Malicious system contract state manipulation could break beacon chain sync (EIP-4788), historical proof generation (EIP-2935), or staking operations (EIP-7002/7251). System contracts trusted to maintain invariants. [S26] [S27] Sources: [S26] ./core/state_processor.go:260-400, [S27] ./params/config.go:1196-1214

trusted_entities.assumption: Sensitive RPC namespaces (admin, debug, personal) restricted to IPC or authenticated connections. [S4] Default HTTP whitelist allows only eth, net, web3. [S4] Account unlocking forbidden over HTTP/WebSocket. [S4] Sources: [S4] https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/interacting-with-geth/rpc
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Exposed debug/admin APIs allow arbitrary code execution (debug_setHead, admin_startRPC), peer manipulation (admin_addPeer), or account access (personal_unlockAccount). Bots scan for open HTTP RPC to exploit. [S4] Geth warns about HTTP exposure and requires explicit --http.api configuration. [S2] Sources: [S2] https://geth.ethereum.org/docs, [S4] https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/interacting-with-geth/rpc

user_flows.title: Transaction Submission and Mempool Admission (eth_sendRawTransaction)
preconditions: User has signed transaction with valid ECDSA signature covering chainID (EIP-155). [S10] Node is synced to chain head. [S28] Sources: [S10] ./core/txpool/validation.go:115-118, [S28] ./eth/handler.go:150-180
steps: 1. User submits RLP-encoded signed transaction via eth_sendRawTransaction RPC. [S29] Transaction decoded from hexutil.Bytes format. [S29] Sources: [S29] ./internal/ethapi/api.go:1800-1850
2. RPC handler calls backend.SendTx() which forwards to TxPool.Add(). [S30] Sources: [S30] ./core/txpool/txpool.go:500-550
3. TxPool routes transaction to appropriate subpool based on type: LegacyPool (types 0x00/0x01/0x02), BlobPool (type 0x03), or future pools. [S31] Sources: [S31] ./core/txpool/txpool.go:200-250

4. Subpool performs stateless validation via ValidateTransaction(): [S32] (a) Check transaction type supported by current fork (Berlin/London/Cancun/Prague). [S32] (b) Verify size under limit (default 128KB, blob pool 256KB). [S33] (c) Validate transaction fields: no negative value, gasFeeCap >= gasTipCap, nonce < 2^64. [S32] (d) Compute intrinsic gas and verify tx.Gas >= intrinsicGas. [S34] (e) For blob transactions (EIP-4844): verify sidecar present, 1-6 blobs, commitments match blob hashes via KZG verification. [S21] Sources: [S21] ./core/txpool/validation.go:190-199, [S32] ./core/txpool/validation.go:61-154, [S33] ./core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:600-650, [S34] ./core/state_transition.go:70-117

5. If stateless validation passes, subpool performs stateful checks: [S35] (a) Verify sender nonce matches or is future (queue vs pending). [S35] (b) Check sender balance >= value + gasLimit * gasFeeCap (+ blobGasFeeCap * blobGas for blob txs). [S36] (c) For blob txs, verify blobGasFeeCap >= current blob base fee. [S37] Sources: [S35] ./core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:700-800, [S36] ./core/state_transition.go:200-250, [S37] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:80-110

6. If all validations pass, transaction inserted into pending or queued map. [S35] Pending transactions have matching nonce and are executable. [S35] Queued transactions have future nonces awaiting predecessor. [S35] Sources: [S35] ./core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:700-800

7. Transaction propagated to P2P peers via TransactionsMsg (0x02) for full transactions under 4KB or NewPooledTransactionHashesMsg (0x08) for hashes of larger transactions. [S38] Sources: [S38] ./eth/handler.go:250-300
8. Peers receiving transaction perform identical validation before adding to their pools. [S32] [S38] Sources: [S32] ./core/txpool/validation.go:61-154, [S38] ./eth/handler.go:250-300
postconditions: Transaction admitted to mempool pending set if nonce matches, or queued set if future nonce. [S35] Transaction available for inclusion in next mined block. [S39] Rejected transactions return error to RPC caller. [S30] Sources: [S30] ./core/txpool/txpool.go:500-550, [S35] ./core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go:700-800, [S39] ./miner/worker.go:800-900

user_flows.title: Block Building and Payload Construction (engine_getPayload)
preconditions: Consensus client previously called engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3 with PayloadAttributes including timestamp, random (prevRandao), suggestedFeeRecipient, withdrawals, and beaconRoot. [S40] PayloadID returned and tracked in localBlocks cache. [S41] Sources: [S40] ./beacon/engine/types.go:55-70, [S41] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:600-650
steps: 1. Consensus client calls engine_getPayloadV3(payloadID) when validator is proposer. [S42] Sources: [S42] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:700-750

2. Engine API retrieves cached Payload from localBlocks queue using payloadID. [S41] Payload contains both empty block (built immediately) and full block (built asynchronously). [S43] Sources: [S41] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:600-650, [S43] ./miner/payload_building.go:80-120

3. If full block not ready, resolve() blocks waiting for miner to complete. [S43] Worker builds block in background via buildPayload(). [S44] Sources: [S43] ./miner/payload_building.go:80-120, [S44] ./miner/worker.go:1000-1100

4. Worker initializes environment with parent state, block header (number, timestamp, baseFee, blobGasUsed, excessBlobGas), and empty transaction list. [S44] Sources: [S44] ./miner/worker.go:1000-1100

5. Worker executes system calls before transactions: [S26] (a) ProcessBeaconBlockRoot(beaconRoot) writes to 0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02 (EIP-4788). [S45] (b) ProcessParentBlockHash(parentHash) writes to 0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935 (EIP-2935). [S46] (c) ProcessWithdrawalQueue() reads withdrawal requests from 0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002 (EIP-7002). [S47] (d) ProcessConsolidationQueue() reads consolidation requests from 0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251 (EIP-7251). [S48] Sources: [S26] ./core/state_processor.go:260-400, [S45] ./core/state_processor.go:440-480, [S46] ./core/state_processor.go:480-520, [S47] ./core/state_processor.go:520-560, [S48] ./core/state_processor.go:560-600

6. Worker processes withdrawals from PayloadAttributes: [S49] For each withdrawal, credit withdrawal.Amount to withdrawal.Address (creating account if needed). [S49] No gas cost for withdrawals. [S49] Sources: [S49] ./core/state_processor.go:350-390

7. Worker fills block with transactions from TxPool pending set: [S50] (a) Select transactions by effective priority fee (min(maxFeePerGas - baseFee, maxPriorityFeePerGas)). [S51] (b) Order transactions within same account by nonce. [S51] (c) For each transaction: execute via ApplyTransaction(), accumulate gas used, generate receipt, append transaction to block. [S52] (d) Stop when gas limit reached, blob limit reached, or block size would exceed 8MB (EIP-7934). [S53] (e) Track blob count separately (max 6 for Cancun, configurable for later forks). [S54] Sources: [S50] ./miner/worker.go:1100-1200, [S51] ./miner/ordering.go:40-90, [S52] ./core/state_processor.go:150-200, [S53] ./core/block_validator.go:90-100, [S54] ./params/config.go:369-418

8. Worker finalizes block: [S55] (a) Compute state root via stateDB.Commit(). [S56] (b) Compute receipts root from receipt trie. [S57] (c) Compute logs bloom filter. [S57] (d) For Prague+, compute requests hash from execution requests (deposits from EIP-6110, withdrawals from EIP-7002, consolidations from EIP-7251). [S58] (e) Assemble header with all computed fields. [S55] Sources: [S55] ./miner/worker.go:1200-1250, [S56] ./core/state/statedb.go:650-700, [S57] ./core/types/receipt.go:200-250, [S58] ./core/state_processor.go:600-650

9. Worker packages block into ExecutionPayloadEnvelope with blockValue (sum of transaction fees), blobsBundle (commitments/proofs/blobs for blob transactions), and requests array. [S59] Sources: [S59] ./beacon/engine/types.go:118-150
10. Engine API returns envelope to consensus client. [S42] Consensus client broadcasts block to beacon network. [S42] Sources: [S42] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:700-750
postconditions: Executable payload with valid state root, receipts root, and all required fields returned. [S42] Payload cached in remoteBlocks for later validation if received from network. [S41] Block ready for consensus layer proposal. [S42] Sources: [S41] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:600-650, [S42] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:700-750

user_flows.title: Payload Validation and Import (engine_newPayload)
preconditions: Consensus client received block from beacon network peer. [S60] Block contains ExecutableData with all required fields (parentHash, feeRecipient, stateRoot, receiptsRoot, transactions, etc.). [S61] Sources: [S60] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:900-950, [S61] ./beacon/engine/types.go:72-94
steps: 1. Consensus client calls engine_newPayloadV3(executableData, expectedBlobVersionedHashes, parentBeaconBlockRoot) or V4 with executionRequests. [S60] Sources: [S60] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:900-950

2. Engine API validates payload version matches fork: [S62] (a) V1 for Paris (no withdrawals/beaconRoot). [S62] (b) V2 for Shanghai (adds withdrawals). [S62] (c) V3 for Cancun (adds blobGasUsed/excessBlobGas). [S62] (d) V4 for Prague (adds requests). [S62] Sources: [S62] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:950-1000

3. Engine API checks if block already known via blockchain.GetBlockByHash(). [S63] If known valid, return VALID status immediately. [S63] If known invalid (in invalidBlocksHits map), return INVALID with last valid hash. [S64] Sources: [S63] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1000-1020, [S64] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:120-130
4. Engine API verifies parent exists in local chain. [S63] If parent unknown, return SYNCING status triggering beacon sync. [S63] Sources: [S63] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1000-1020

5. Engine API constructs Block from ExecutableData: [S65] (a) Decode transactions from [][]byte to []*types.Transaction. [S65] (b) Verify block hash matches executableData.BlockHash. [S66] (c) Verify blob versioned hashes match transaction blob hashes. [S67] Sources: [S65] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1050-1100, [S66] ./core/types/block.go:200-230, [S67] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1100-1120

6. Engine API calls blockchain.InsertBlockWithoutSetHead() for optimistic validation. [S68] Block not set as head until forkchoice update confirms. [S68] Sources: [S68] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1150-1180

7. BlockValidator.ValidateBody() performs structural validation: [S69] (a) Verify transactions and uncles in allowed ranges (uncles must be empty post-merge). [S69] (b) Verify transaction root matches computed trie root. [S70] (c) Verify uncle hash matches (must be empty hash post-merge). [S69] (d) For Shanghai+, verify withdrawals root matches. [S71] (e) For Cancun+, verify blob gas usage matches sum of transaction blob gas. [S72] Sources: [S69] ./core/block_validator.go:50-90, [S70] ./core/types/block.go:250-280, [S71] ./core/block_validator.go:100-120, [S72] ./core/block_validator.go:120-140

8. StateProcessor.Process() executes block transactions: [S73] (a) Initialize state from parent block. [S74] (b) Execute system calls (beacon root, parent hash, withdrawals, consolidations). [S26] (c) For each transaction: call ApplyTransaction() which invokes state transition, updates state, generates receipt. [S75] (d) Process withdrawals by crediting amounts. [S49] (e) Finalize block via consensus engine (no-op for PoS). [S76] Sources: [S26] ./core/state_processor.go:260-400, [S49] ./core/state_processor.go:350-390, [S73] ./core/state_processor.go:80-150, [S74] ./core/state/statedb.go:400-450, [S75] ./core/state_processor.go:150-200, [S76] ./core/state_processor.go:200-250

9. BlockValidator.ValidateState() verifies execution results: [S77] (a) Verify total gas used matches header.GasUsed. [S77] (b) Verify receipts root matches header.ReceiptsRoot. [S78] (c) Verify logs bloom filter matches header.Bloom. [S78] (d) Verify state root matches header.Root. [S79] (e) For Prague+, verify requests hash matches header.RequestsHash. [S80] Sources: [S77] ./core/block_validator.go:140-160, [S78] ./core/block_validator.go:160-175, [S79] ./core/block_validator.go:175-185, [S80] ./core/block_validator.go:185-196

10. If validation succeeds, block inserted into chain (pending fork choice confirmation). [S68] Engine API returns VALID status with latest valid hash. [S81] Sources: [S68] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1150-1180, [S81] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1200-1220

11. If validation fails, block added to invalidBlocksHits map with hit count 1. [S64] Engine API returns INVALID status with last valid hash (parent if available). [S82] Sources: [S64] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:120-130, [S82] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1220-1250
postconditions: Valid payload inserted into chain as pending head, awaiting fork choice update. [S68] Invalid payload rejected and tracked ephemerally. [S64] Consensus client uses status (VALID/INVALID/SYNCING) to update fork choice. [S81] Sources: [S64] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:120-130, [S68] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1150-1180, [S81] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1200-1220

user_flows.title: Fork Choice Update and Chain Reorganization (engine_forkchoiceUpdated)
preconditions: Consensus client finalized beacon chain fork choice. [S83] ForkchoiceStateV1 contains headBlockHash, safeBlockHash, and finalizedBlockHash. [S84] All referenced blocks previously validated via engine_newPayload. [S85] Sources: [S83] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:162-200, [S84] ./beacon/engine/types.go:30-50, [S85] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1300-1330
steps: 1. Consensus client calls engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3(forkchoiceState, payloadAttributes) or V2 for earlier forks. [S83] PayloadAttributes optional (only present when node is proposer). [S40] Sources: [S40] ./beacon/engine/types.go:55-70, [S83] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:162-200

2. Engine API validates fork choice state: [S86] (a) Verify headBlockHash exists in local chain (previously validated). [S86] (b) Verify safeBlockHash and finalizedBlockHash exist and are ancestors of head. [S86] (c) If any block missing, return SYNCING to trigger sync. [S86] Sources: [S86] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1330-1380
3. Engine API checks if headBlockHash already current head. [S87] If yes and no payloadAttributes, return SUCCESS immediately. [S87] Sources: [S87] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1380-1400

4. Engine API initiates chain reorganization via blockchain.SetHead(headBlockHash): [S88] (a) If new head is descendant of current head (forward progress), append new blocks. [S88] (b) If new head on different branch (reorg), identify common ancestor and rewind to it. [S89] (c) Re-execute transactions in new branch blocks to update state. [S90] (d) Update current head pointer to new head. [S88] Sources: [S88] ./core/blockchain.go:1500-1600, [S89] ./core/blockchain.go:1600-1700, [S90] ./core/blockchain.go:1700-1800

5. Engine API updates safe and finalized block markers: [S91] (a) Set blockchain.safeBlockHash to forkchoiceState.safeBlockHash. [S91] (b) Set blockchain.finalizedBlockHash to forkchoiceState.finalizedBlockHash. [S91] (c) Prune blocks below finalized (optional, controlled by config). [S92] Sources: [S91] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1450-1480, [S92] ./core/blockchain.go:1900-1950

6. If payloadAttributes provided (node is proposer), initiate block building: [S93] (a) Validate payload attributes for current fork (V1: no withdrawals/beaconRoot, V2: adds withdrawals, V3: adds beaconRoot). [S94] (b) Generate payloadID = SHA256(parentHash || timestamp || random || feeRecipient || withdrawals || beaconRoot). [S95] (c) Start async payload building via miner.BuildPayload(). [S96] (d) Cache empty payload immediately in localBlocks. [S97] Sources: [S93] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1500-1550, [S94] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:174-200, [S95] ./miner/payload_building.go:50-80, [S96] ./miner/worker.go:1000-1100, [S97] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1550-1580
7. Engine API returns ForkChoiceResponse with status SUCCESS or SYNCING. [S98] If payload building initiated, response includes payloadID. [S98] Sources: [S98] ./eth/catalyst/api.go:1600-1630

user_flows.title: EIP-1559 Dynamic Fee Transaction Execution
preconditions: Transaction type 0x02 (DynamicFeeTx) with gasFeeCap, gasTipCap, and standard fields. [S100] Current block has baseFeePerGas from parent (London fork active). [S101] Transaction admitted to mempool with gasFeeCap >= baseFee. [S102] Sources: [S100] ./core/types/tx_dynamic_fee.go:30-60, [S101] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-50, [S102] ./core/txpool/validation.go:142-145
steps: 1. Miner selects transaction for block inclusion based on effective priority fee: effectiveTip = min(gasFeeCap - baseFee, gasTipCap). [S103] Higher effectiveTip transactions prioritized. [S104] Sources: [S103] ./core/types/transaction.go:280-310, [S104] ./miner/ordering.go:40-70

2. State transition begins via ApplyTransaction(): [S105] (a) Convert transaction to Message via TransactionToMessage(). [S106] (b) Compute effective gas price: effectiveGasPrice = min(gasFeeCap, gasTipCap + baseFee). [S107] Sources: [S105] ./core/state_processor.go:150-180, [S106] ./core/state_transition.go:175-200, [S107] ./core/state_transition.go:193-199

3. Validate sender account state: [S108] (a) Check nonce matches transaction nonce. [S108] (b) Check balance >= value + gasLimit * gasFeeCap (worst case gas cost). [S109] Sources: [S108] ./core/state_transition.go:250-280, [S109] ./core/state_transition.go:280-300

4. Buy gas upfront: deduct gasLimit * effectiveGasPrice from sender balance. [S110] Create gas pool with gasLimit available. [S111] Sources: [S110] ./core/state_transition.go:300-320, [S111] ./core/state_transition.go:320-330

5. Execute transaction: [S112] (a) If contract creation (to == nil), deploy new contract with CREATE opcode semantics. [S113] (b) If message call, invoke target contract or transfer value to EOA. [S114] (c) EVM executes bytecode with gas metering, updating state. [S115] Sources: [S112] ./core/state_transition.go:330-370, [S113] ./core/vm/evm.go:400-450, [S114] ./core/vm/evm.go:200-250, [S115] ./core/vm/interpreter.go:120-200

6. Calculate gas refund: [S116] (a) Compute unused gas: gasRefund = gasLimit - gasUsed. [S116] (b) Add SSTORE refunds (capped at gasUsed / 5 per EIP-3529). [S117] (c) Refund unused gas to sender: refund gasRefund * effectiveGasPrice. [S118] Sources: [S116] ./core/state_transition.go:380-400, [S117] ./core/vm/operations_acl.go:120-150, [S118] ./core/state_transition.go:400-420

7. Pay miner: [S119] (a) Compute miner tip: minerTip = gasUsed * effectiveTip. [S119] (b) Credit minerTip to block coinbase (feeRecipient). [S120] (c) Burn base fee: baseBurn = gasUsed * baseFee (not credited to any account). [S121] Sources: [S119] ./core/state_transition.go:420-440, [S120] ./core/state_transition.go:440-450, [S121] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:70-90

8. Generate receipt with status, gasUsed, logs, and bloom filter. [S122] Append transaction and receipt to block. [S123] Sources: [S122] ./core/state_processor.go:180-200, [S123] ./core/state_processor.go:200-220
postconditions: Transaction executed with state changes committed. [S124] Gas consumed, sender debited, miner credited tip, base fee burned. [S119] [S121] Receipt generated and stored. [S122] Sources: [S119] ./core/state_transition.go:420-440, [S121] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:70-90, [S122] ./core/state_processor.go:180-200, [S124] ./core/state/statedb.go:550-600

user_flows.title: EIP-4844 Blob Transaction Processing
preconditions: Transaction type 0x03 (BlobTx) with blobVersionedHashes, maxFeePerBlobGas, and BlobTxSidecar containing blobs/commitments/proofs. [S125] Cancun fork active. [S126] Blob base fee calculated from parent excessBlobGas. [S127] Sources: [S125] ./core/types/tx_blob.go:40-80, [S126] ./core/txpool/validation.go:82-84, [S127] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:80-110
steps: 1. User submits blob transaction with 1-6 blobs (131,072 bytes each). [S128] Each blob has KZG commitment and proof. [S129] Sources: [S128] ./core/txpool/validation.go:173-175, [S129] ./core/types/tx_blob.go:100-130

2. BlobPool validates blob transaction: [S130] (a) Verify sidecar present (blobs required for mempool admission). [S131] (b) Verify maxFeePerBlobGas >= current blob base fee. [S132] (c) Verify number of blobs matches blobVersionedHashes length. [S133] (d) For each blob: compute commitment hash, verify matches blobVersionedHashes[i]. [S134] (e) Verify KZG proof for each blob: VerifyBlobProof(blob, commitment, proof). [S135] Sources: [S130] ./core/txpool/validation.go:157-188, [S131] ./core/txpool/validation.go:159-162, [S132] ./core/txpool/validation.go:163-166, [S133] ./core/txpool/validation.go:176-178, [S134] ./core/types/tx_blob.go:200-230, [S135] ./crypto/kzg4844/kzg4844.go:140-170

3. Blob transaction propagated to peers with sidecar. [S136] Blobs stored temporarily (pruned after ~18 days). [S137] Sources: [S136] ./eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go:200-250, [S137] ./eth/ethconfig/config.go:80-100

4. Miner includes blob transaction in block payload: [S138] (a) Track blob count toward block blob limit (default 6). [S139] (b) Append blob transaction to block transactions list. [S140] (c) Include blobs in BlobsBundle of ExecutionPayloadEnvelope. [S141] Sources: [S138] ./miner/worker.go:1150-1180, [S139] ./params/config.go:369-418, [S140] ./miner/worker.go:1200-1220, [S141] ./beacon/engine/types.go:130-150

5. State transition for blob transaction: [S142] (a) Buy gas as standard transaction: deduct gasLimit * effectiveGasPrice. [S143] (b) Buy blob gas: deduct blobCount * blobGasPerBlob * min(maxFeePerBlobGas, blobBaseFee). [S144] (c) Execute transaction normally (blobs not directly accessible to EVM, only versioned hashes in BLOBHASH opcode). [S145] (d) Refund unused execution gas. [S146] (e) Burn blob gas payment (not refunded, not credited to miner). [S147] Sources: [S142] ./core/state_transition.go:330-370, [S143] ./core/state_transition.go:300-320, [S144] ./core/state_transition.go:320-330, [S145] ./core/vm/instructions.go:700-720, [S146] ./core/state_transition.go:380-400, [S147] ./core/state_transition.go:450-470

6. Block validator verifies blob gas usage: [S148] (a) Sum blobGasUsed from all blob transactions. [S148] (b) Verify header.BlobGasUsed matches computed sum. [S149] (c) Verify header.ExcessBlobGas computed correctly from parent per EIP-4844 formula. [S150] Sources: [S148] ./core/block_validator.go:120-135, [S149] ./core/block_validator.go:135-140, [S150] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:110-140

7. Update blob base fee for next block: [S151] blobBaseFee = blobFeePerGas(excessBlobGas) where excessBlobGas accumulates deviation from target blob count. [S152] Formula: excessBlobGas_new = max(0, excessBlobGas + blobGasUsed - targetBlobGas). [S153] Sources: [S151] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:80-110, [S152] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:50-80, [S153] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:110-140
postconditions: Blob transaction executed with gas and blob gas consumed. [S142] [S144] Blobs available for data availability sampling by consensus layer. [S154] Blob gas payment burned, adjusting next block's blob base fee. [S151] Sources: [S142] ./core/state_transition.go:330-370, [S144] ./core/state_transition.go:320-330, [S151] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:80-110, [S154] ./eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go:250-280

algorithms.name: EIP-1559 Base Fee Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Adjust base fee per block to target 50% gas usage, making fees more predictable and burning base fee to reduce ETH supply. [S12] Sources: [S12] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-50
algorithms.notes: BaseFeeChangeDenominator = 8 bounds max base fee change to ±12.5% per block. [S155] ElasticityMultiplier = 2 allows blocks to use up to 2x target gas. [S156] Base fee always >= 0, never negative. [S12] Initial base fee at London fork: 1,000,000,000 wei (1 gwei). [S157] Sources: [S12] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-70, [S155] ./params/protocol_params.go:30-40, [S156] ./params/protocol_params.go:40-50, [S157] ./params/protocol_params.go:50-60

algorithms.name: EIP-4844 Blob Base Fee Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Adjust blob gas price exponentially to target 3 blobs per block (Cancun) or higher targets in later forks, maintaining data availability cost stability. [S151] Sources: [S151] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:50-80
algorithms.complexity: O(k) where k is number of Taylor series iterations (typically < 20), bounded by excessBlobGas magnitude
algorithms.notes: Blob config parameters vary by fork: Cancun (target=3, max=6, updateFraction=3338477), Prague (target=6, max=9, updateFraction=5007716), Osaka/BPO1/BPO2 have further increases. [S158] Minimum blob gas price always 1 wei. [S159] Blob gas payments burned, not refunded. [S147] UpdateFraction controls exponential curve steepness. [S151] Sources: [S147] ./core/state_transition.go:450-470, [S151] ./consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:50-80, [S158] ./params/config.go:369-418, [S159] ./params/protocol_params.go:120-130

algorithms.name: Intrinsic Gas Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Compute minimum gas required for transaction before EVM execution, preventing underpriced transactions and ensuring resource accountability. [S34] Sources: [S34] ./core/state_transition.go:70-117
algorithms.complexity: O(n) where n = len(data), for counting zero bytes. Access list is O(m) for m addresses/keys.
algorithms.notes: Transaction rejected if gas < intrinsicGas. [S160] EIP-2028 reduced non-zero byte cost from 68 to 16 gas to support data-heavy use cases. [S161] EIP-3860 adds init code cost to prevent DoS via large contract deployments. [S162] Access list preloads storage to reduce execution gas. [S163] Sources: [S34] ./core/state_transition.go:70-117, [S160] ./core/txpool/validation.go:129-131, [S161] ./params/protocol_params.go:80-90, [S162] ./params/protocol_params.go:100-110, [S163] ./core/vm/operations_acl.go:30-50

algorithms.name: Transaction Effective Priority Fee
algorithms.purpose: Rank transactions for block inclusion, prioritizing those paying higher tips to miners while respecting base fee floor. [S103] Sources: [S103] ./core/types/transaction.go:280-310
algorithms.complexity: O(1) per transaction for tip calculation. O(n log n) for sorting n transactions.
algorithms.notes: Miners maximize revenue by selecting high-tip transactions. [S164] Base fee burned, so not factor in miner incentive. [S121] Legacy transactions (pre-EIP-1559) treated as gasPrice = min(gasPrice, gasFeeCap) for compatibility. [S165] Sources: [S103] ./core/types/transaction.go:280-310, [S121] ./consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:70-90, [S164] ./miner/ordering.go:70-90, [S165] ./core/types/transaction.go:310-340

algorithms.name: EVM Gas Metering and Refund
algorithms.purpose: Track gas consumption during EVM execution to prevent DoS, ensure deterministic costs, and refund unused gas to sender. [S18] Sources: [S18] ./core/vm/gas_table.go:50-150
algorithms.complexity: O(n) where n = number of opcodes executed. Memory expansion is O(m) for m bytes allocated.
algorithms.notes: EIP-2929 introduced access lists to reduce gas for warm storage (100 vs 2100). [S166] EIP-3529 reduced max refund from 50% to 20% (1/5) to prevent gas token abuse. [S167] EIP-1884 increased SLOAD cost from 200 to 800 (Istanbul). [S168] Memory expansion cost quadratic to prevent DoS via large allocations. [S169] Sources: [S20] ./core/vm/operations_acl.go:30-80, [S166] ./params/protocol_params.go:140-150, [S167] ./params/protocol_params.go:150-160, [S168] ./params/protocol_params.go:90-100, [S169] ./core/vm/gas_table.go:150-180

algorithms.name: Block Validation (ValidateBody and ValidateState)
algorithms.purpose: Ensure received block conforms to consensus rules before chain incorporation, preventing invalid state transitions and maintaining network consistency. [S69] [S77] Sources: [S69] ./core/block_validator.go:50-90, [S77] ./core/block_validator.go:140-160
algorithms.complexity: O(n) for n transactions (transaction root O(n log n) for merkle tree). State root computation dominates: O(k) for k state changes.
algorithms.notes: ValidateBody runs before state execution (cheap pre-filter). [S170] ValidateState runs after execution (expensive, final verification). [S171] State root mismatch most common validation failure, indicates non-determinism or bug. [S172] DeriveSha uses Merkle Patricia Trie (keccak256 hashing). [S173] Sources: [S8] ./core/block_validator.go:50-140, [S170] ./core/block_validator.go:50-60, [S171] ./core/block_validator.go:175-185, [S172] ./core/block_validator.go:180-190, [S173] ./core/types/block.go:250-280

algorithms.name: State Root Computation (Merkle Patricia Trie)
algorithms.purpose: Generate cryptographic commitment to world state enabling efficient state verification and fraud proofs. [S56] Sources: [S56] ./core/state/statedb.go:650-700
algorithms.complexity: O(n log m) where n = modified accounts, m = total accounts. Storage root is O(k log s) for k modified slots, s total slots per account.
algorithms.notes: Geth uses Path-based State Scheme (PBSS) for efficient trie storage. [S175] State trie pruning keeps only last 128 blocks in memory (TriesInMemory). [S176] Verkle trees (EIP-6800) planned to replace MPT for O(log n) witness generation. [S177] Trie nodes cached to avoid redundant hashing. [S178] Sources: [S174] ./triedb/database.go:100-200, [S175] ./triedb/pathdb/database.go:50-100, [S176] ./core/state/statedb.go:80-100, [S177] ./trie/verkle.go:40-80, [S178] ./triedb/database.go:200-250

algorithms.name: KZG Commitment Verification (EIP-4844)
algorithms.purpose: Verify polynomial commitment for blob data matches claimed commitment using KZG proof, ensuring data availability without downloading full blob. [S21] Sources: [S21] ./core/txpool/validation.go:190-199
algorithms.complexity: O(n) for n field elements in blob (4096). Pairing operations are expensive constant-time BLS12-381 operations.
algorithms.notes: Trusted setup ceremony performed once, parameters embedded in client. [S180] KZG proofs enable data availability sampling (DAS) without full blob download. [S181] Blob hash is SHA256(versionByte || commitment). [S182] Osaka fork (EIP-PeerDAS) introduces cell-based proofs for more efficient DAS.
